title: Granular route affinity + retention ledger with compliance export
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Provide customers with a UI + API to declare per-tenant route affinity (soft/hard), configure retention policies per-route, and generate a tamper-evident ledger export (audit bundle) that proves where and how data was routed and retained for a given time window.
acceptance_criteria: UI: Tenant-level 'Routing & Retention' page allowing selection of primary region, fallback order, and affinity mode (soft/hard) — changes saved and displayed in audit log
API: New PATCH /tenants/:id/residency accepts {primary_region, fallback_regions, affinity_mode, retention_days, retention_policy_id} and returns 200 with effective config and change_id
Enforcement: Requests to hosted endpoints must route according to policy; when capacity unavailable for hard affinity -> return 409 with reason unless tenant opt-in for cross-region fallback
Retention: Retention rules applied to request payloads and derived artifacts (embeddings, cached KV) with TTL enforcement and deletion jobs observed in ledger

Evidence export: Admin can request a signed export (zip) for a time range containing: change history, routing traces (sampled), retention deletion records, and verification signature; export generation must complete within SLA (30 min) for 90th percentile of most tenants
Security: Evidence export stored encrypted with customer KMS key when configured; logs show KMS operations and ACLs set to tenant-admins
Telemetry: Console dashboard surfaces token-level cost delta when hard affinity is enabled vs default routing based on historical 30-day baseline
Backward compatibility: Existing tenants with no residency config should default to 'global' soft-affinity and be handled without disruption
proposal: Implement a tenant residency declaration assistant in the Console combined with a residency API. Persist an immutable 'residency ledger' (append-only events) in the compliance store. Wire routing policy to the smart router to prefer primary region and enforce hard-affinity via admission checks. Capture retention lifecycle events (create/delete) and include them in a signed evidence bundle using Redwood's signing service. Support optional KMS-backed encryption for exports.
tradeoffs: Hard-affinity increases request failure surface under capacity pressure — we will return explicit errors so customers can choose opt-in fallbacks; alternative is automatic fallback which weakens residency guarantees
Keeping a full raw-request trace in evidence increases bundle size and privacy risk — we will store sampled traces plus hashed fingerprints for verification
Signed exports add operational work (signing, key rotation) and latency for bundle creation; we limit exports to a fixed window and support background generation to meet SLA
engineering_notes: Frontend: Add ResidencyEditor component under Console -> Tenant Settings; use feature flag residency.ui.v1
Backend: New service tenancy-residency-svc with append-only ledger table (ledger_id, tenant_id, event_type, payload_hash, signed_digest, created_at)
Router: Smart router will accept a residency header from tenancy-residency-svc and apply routing policy; admission controller will implement hard-affinity check returning 409 if unsatisfiable
DB: Retention jobs must emit deletion events and link to ledger change_id for traceability
Export: Evidence generator aggregates ledger rows + sampled traces, signs bundle with signing-service, uploads to secure s3 path, optionally encrypts with customer KMS key
qa_plan: Unit tests for API validation and ledger append semantics
Integration tests: simulate capacity pressure to verify hard-affinity 409 behavior and soft-affinity fallbacks
E2E: Console flows to set residency and request evidence export; verify bundle integrity and signatures
Load test: generate evidence exports for 1000 tenants concurrently to validate background job scaling and 30 min SLA
rollout_plan: Feature-gate residency.ui.v1 and residency.api.v1 behind 'residency-beta' toggle. Phase 1: internal teams + selected customers (canary tenants). Phase 2: opt-in public beta. Phase 3: general availability after 6 weeks of telemetry and at least one successful audit export for an enterprise customer.
